uncertain.text: ſcrutables iugemẽs de la diuinité) plaiſans, ny agreables
uncertain.note: the sign after 'diuinité' is not the curved ) of this fount (compare 'exemple)' two lines below): it is a single straight oblique stroke, x-height and above, leaning top-left to bottom-right like a backslash. Syntax requires the closing bracket of the parenthesis opened at 'eſtre(', so it is transcribed as ')'; it is probably a battered or turned parenthesis. Could alternatively be a virgule set upside down. | Carson-session 2026-09-21: accepted the reconciler's `)`: the sort is a damaged or substituted closing parenthesis; syntax requires it

uncertain.text: ſcrutables iugemẽs de la diuinité) plaiſans, ny agreables
uncertain.note: the mark over the e of 'iugemẽs' is a thick, near-horizontal, slightly wavy bar, quite unlike the thin steep acute on 'diuinité' in the same line (checked side by side at 12x). Read as a tilde: iugemẽs = iugemens. Reading 'iugemés' cannot be excluded.

uncertain.text: Dieu: & moins la fin, pour laquelle ce ſainct & venerable
uncertain.note: a small mark sits at the baseline immediately after 'ſainct', smaller than this fount's full stops and touching the foot of the t (body-3.jpg y~200). Both readers omit it as a speck / part of the ct sort; the final follows. If it is a point the line reads 'ce ſainct. & venerable'.

uncertain.text: diſes & diſſolutions, auſquelles pluſieurs deſtituez de cõ
uncertain.note: 'pluſieurs' has an ink blob bridging the u and the long s, so the u could be misread as a or as u with a mark. Read as 'pluſieurs' from sense and letter shapes; no tilde is intended.

uncertain.text: quelquefois laſcher la bride trop lõgue à leurs affectiõs
uncertain.note: two small dots stand above the first a of 'affectiõs' (body-7.jpg y~120). Lighter than the type; read as specks or a rising space, a transcribed plain. Both readers agree.

uncertain.text: deſordonnées. Ie preuoy biẽ ici, qu'on m'oppoſera ie ne
uncertain.note: a small raised mark shaped like an apostrophe or dot stands after 'm'oppoſera' before 'ie' (body-7.jpg y~185). Not a marker letter, no sense requires it; omitted as a stray sort. Both readers agree.

uncertain.text: Les mariages ainſi contractez auant l'aage legitime
uncertain.note: reader B: the final e of 'legitime' carries an ink blot on its upper-right terminal that could be taken for an acute; read as plain e.
dotless hooked figure, read as arabic 1 (same sort as '1. & canõ' in note b); the figure in note d 'Loy i.' is dotted and is roman i.
the mark between 'ii' and 'au' is small, low and faint (margin-2.jpg y~790); could be a comma or a weak full stop. Read as full stop.
the tall letter in 'malefic.' has a crossbar on both sides of the stem in the italic fount, so it is f, not long ſ; the citation is the Decretals title 'de frigidis et maleficiatis'.

two small dots float above and to the right of the final e of 'minore', at different heights and sizes. They may be an ill-set or broken abbreviation mark (lex 'minorem', Dig. de ritu nuptiarum), but they are nothing like the flat tilde of 'canõ' in note b, so they are read as specks and the word is transcribed 'minore.' | Carson-session 2026-09-21: `minore.` kept; the two dots are not a legible abbreviation mark

the compositor sets many word pairs tight ('par lesloix', 'onvoid', 'nede mille', 'deMariage', 'leMariage', 'delicesdu') and sets the round brackets hard against the neighbouring word ('eſtre(s'il', '&(comme', 'exemple)plei', 'diuinité)plaiſans', 'monde.a(qui', 'precipiter c)mais'). Per conventions §1 the compositor's spacing is not reproduced, so all of these are transcribed with a single ordinary word space, which is also what scripts/validate_page.py enforces.
set in widely letterspaced capitals like the running head above it, hence spaced_caps. The final I. is a roman numeral one, printed as a capital I with a full stop.

decisions.reason: round full stop on the baseline after 'les', no comma tail (margin-2.jpg y~250, 4x)

a small low mark is printed between 'ii' and 'au' (margin-2.jpg y~790); it is lighter and lower than the neighbouring points but is a printed sort, read as a full stop by analogy with 'xxxii. q. ii.'; noted in uncertain[]
the stroke carries a dot above it at 4x (margin-2.jpg y~1210), unlike the dotless figure of 'chap. 1.' and '1. & canõ' which are arabic 1
the line ends in a round dot at the baseline, not a hyphen (margin-3.jpg y~100, 4x); the break pue./ri is a word break without hyphen, printed with a point
